subject: Post-call: Trial planning & success metrics for DataSilo POC
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Leah Torres <leah.torres@datasilo.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call: Trial planning & success metrics for DataSilo POC

Thanks again for your time this morning, Leah — appreciate the candid product context and the priorities you shared. Quick written recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before we kick off the 2-week trial.

Call highlights / goals
- Customer goal: extract structured metadata from ingestion pipeline and surface summaries for analysts (reduce review time).
- Trial objective: validate model accuracy on your real sample workload and confirm cost & latency at production-scale patterns.

Proposed success criteria (please confirm):
- Latency: P95 end-to-end inference latency <= 250ms for single-turn queries on our dedicated endpoint (sample size: 1k requests across your spike windows).
- Throughput: Sustained 20 req/s with bursts to 50 req/s for short windows (30s) without >5% error rate.
- Cost: avg cost/token <= $0.0008 for generation paths used in the trial (we'll publish a token breakdown per prompt set).
- Quality: labeled precision >= 90% and human evaluation mean score >= 4.2/5 on the judged sample (we'll provide an eval rubric and initial baseline).

Operational asks / readiness items
1) Confirm sample workload: you mentioned a 10k-record anonymized sample — please upload the CSV we discussed (datasilo-sample-workload.csv) to the Drive link or reply with a shared S3 path.
2) Data transfer & privacy: confirm whether we should use a temporary S3 bucket or direct upload to our secure intake (we support both).
3) SSO & access: request for a test user: leah.torres@datasilo.ai (we'll provision console access).
4) Measurement window: suggest we run the trial over 48 hours to capture typical traffic and a peak window; confirm if that works.

Timeline (tentative)
- Tue 8/18: finalize scope + sample workload upload (today).
- Wed 8/19: infra onboarding + baseline smoke run.
- Thu-Fri 8/20-8/21: 48-hour trial window + evaluation.
- Mon 8/24: readout + recommended next steps.

Owners
- Redwood infra & run: Ben Carter (ben.carter@redwood.ai) — performance tuning and endpoint setup.
- Onboarding & eval design: Camila Reyes (camila.reyes@redwood.ai) — will own eval rubric and human scoring.
- Customer success / commercial: Priyom Das (priyom.das@redwood.ai) — PM and deal owner.

Attachments: datasilo-poc-scope.pdf (scope doc), datasilo-sample-workload.csv (placeholder).

Next step ask: can you confirm the sample upload and whether the 48-hour window looks acceptable? If so we’ll lock times and provision infra.

Thanks,
Priyom

From: Leah Torres <leah.torres@datasilo.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>, DataSilo Evaluation <eval@datasilo.ai>
Date: 2026-08-18T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Trial planning & success metrics for DataSilo POC

Thanks, Priyom — this is great and captures everything we talked about. A few quick clarifications from our side: 

- Sample workload: we can upload a redacted 12k-row CSV to the Drive link by EOD. We'll strip PII but keep the original payload distribution.
- Latency: our internal product team prefers a slightly looser P95 target of 300ms given our end-to-end enrichment steps; would Redwood be comfortable with 300ms P95 for the first trial, with a stretch goal of 250ms?
- Measurement window: the 48-hour window is fine, but can we ensure one of the days includes our morning ingest spike (around 10:30am PST)?
- Quality rubric: the 90% threshold seems aggressive for the first pass; can we agree on a baseline readout first and then set a firm gate after the initial run? We want to avoid hard gating until we see the baseline.

Also, one operational ask — our security team will want a short evidence pack for the trial: SOC-2 scoping note + network diagram + retention policy. Can you confirm what Redwood can share for a short (non-SOC) pack?

Appreciate the clear owners. Looking forward to receiving the Drive link.

-Leah
Leah Torres
Head of Product, DataSilo
leah.torres@datasilo.ai | +1 (415) 555-7789

Thanks, Leah — quick responses inline and plan adjustments.

- Latency: 300ms P95 for the initial run is fine; we’ll treat 250ms as a stretch target for later optimization. We’ll document both as part of the readout.
- Peak window: we’ll schedule the 48-hour window to include 10:30am PST; please confirm a preferred 10:00–11:30am slot on either 8/20 or 8/21 for the peak injection.
- Quality baseline: agree to produce a baseline readout first. Camila will run the initial human scoring and share the rubric and baseline numbers immediately after the 48-hour run.

Security evidence pack (what we can share):
- SOC-2: We can provide our SOC-2 Type II report summary page and a short scoping note specific to the trial (no full report inline).
- Network diagram: redacted-high-level network diagram (no VPC IDs) attached to the Drive link.
- Retention & deletion: we provide a trial-specific retention policy (default 30 days) and a deletion checklist we will execute at trial end.

Operational plan / next steps (action items):
1) DataSilo: upload redacted CSV to the Drive link by EOD 8/18 — mark the file as "trial-input".
2) Redwood: Ben to provision dedicated trial endpoint and run a smoke test on 8/19 morning.
3) Redwood: Camila to share eval rubric and human scoring template by 8/19 afternoon.
4) Scheduling: Leah to confirm preferred peak injection window (10:00–11:30am) on 8/20 or 8/21.
5) Security: Priyom will drop the evidence pack Drive folder link in HubSpot.

I’ve attached: datasilo-poc-scope.pdf (scope + infra checklist) and the network_diagram_redacted.png (on Drive).

If all good I’ll start provisioning now.
